question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose `safetyDiagnostics.emit` and retain its resulting metadata in an operator-readable core safety-event store, including the proposed external-plugin manifest authorization model?
rationale: This is a new public plugin/security/data-retention boundary; tests can validate an implementation but cannot choose the long-term contract, retention posture, or whether the core surface should exist.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core contract
options.body: Approve a documented, privacy-bounded plugin emission and retained-query contract, then require proof of the approved end-to-end path.

options.title: Keep core emitters only
options.body: Retain only internal core diagnostics and remove the new public plugin emission, persistence, and operator-query surfaces until a narrower API is designed.

options.title: Route extensions externally
options.body: Move optional exporter, dashboard, and plugin-driven safety workflows to plugin surfaces after identifying any minimal missing core seam.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow core contract
recommendation.body: Approve a documented, privacy-bounded plugin emission and retained-query contract, then require proof of the approved end-to-end path.

likelyOwner.reason: They can clarify the feature’s intended contract and revise the proposal; final acceptance still needs repository-owner sponsorship.
